# OpenShell

**Turn any web app into a native desktop app – managed by a runtime that people *and* AI agents can operate.**

[![CI](https://github.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-stable-orange?logo=rust)
![Tauri 2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tauri-2-24C8DB?logo=tauri)
![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-ready-6E56CF)
![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha-yellow)

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Usage](#using-openshell) · [AI agents](#ai-agents) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md)

</div>

---

OpenShell is an open-source desktop shell built on **Rust and Tauri 2**. You bring a normal web frontend and any
backend – Python, Node.js, Java, C++, Go, Rust, .NET – and describe them in one `openshell.json`. OpenShell runs
everything as a native desktop app: it starts and supervises your services, shows the frontend in a native window,
reloads on code changes, and builds installers. You never write desktop or process-management code.

What makes it different: every OpenShell app is **agent-native**. AI agents (Claude, OpenAI, local models via Ollama /
LM Studio, any MCP client) can *use* the app through its own functions and *develop* it through a controlled,
permission-checked interface – without clicking through the UI.

> **Build the shell once. Build applications on top of it. Let agents use and evolve them.**

## Quick start

**1. Install** – OpenShell consists of two binaries: `openshell` (CLI) and `openshell-desktop` (the shell).

```bash
# from source (requires Rust; on Linux also the Tauri system packages, see docs/getting-started.md)
git clone https://github.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA.git openshell
cd openshell
cargo build --release
# then put target/release on your PATH (both binaries must stay in the same folder)
```

Prebuilt binaries: once a release is published, use `scripts/install.sh` (macOS/Linux) or `scripts/install.ps1`
(Windows), or download them from the [releases page](https://github.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA/releases).

**2. Create and run an app**

```bash
openshell create my-app          # HTML/JS frontend + Python backend, no other installs needed
cd my-app
openshell dev                    # opens the native window, streams logs, hot-reloads on changes
```

**3. Make it yours** – edit `web/` or `backend/`. The window reloads and the backend restarts automatically.
Other stacks: `openshell create --list` (React, Vue, Svelte, Node.js, Go, Java, C++). Or pick only the building
blocks you need:

```bash
openshell create notes --with frontend,database     # UI + built-in SQLite, no backend
openshell create tools --with functions             # functions for AI agents only – no UI, no server
openshell add backend --lang node                   # add blocks later, in any order
```

**4. Ship it**

```bash
openshell package                # → Windows setup.exe / macOS .dmg / Linux .deb + .AppImage
```

**5. Let AI use it**

```bash
claude mcp add my-app -- openshell mcp --app --start --project .
# "Add a todo 'call the bank' to my app" – the agent calls the app's own add_todo function
```

## How it works

```
             people                                    AI agents (Claude, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, any MCP client)
                │                                                    │
        ┌───────▼────────────────────────────────────────────────────▼────────┐
        │  OpenShell desktop shell (Tauri 2)                                    │
        │  native window + WebView · tray · notifications · approval dialogs   │
        │  ┌───────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────────────┐ │
        │  │ Runtime Manager           │   │ Agent Interaction Layer          │ │
        │  │ start · health · restart  │   │ MCP + HTTP tools · UI bridge     │ │
        │  │ build · logs · metrics    │   │ capabilities · OpenAPI import    │ │
        │  │ ports · file watching     │   │ permissions · approvals · audit  │ │
        │  └─────────────┬─────────────┘   └─────────────────────────────────┘ │
        └────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                         │ manages separate processes – never compiled into the shell
     ┌────────────┬──────┴──────┬────────────┬──────────────┐
     ▼            ▼             ▼            ▼              ▼
  frontend     backend       database     worker      local AI server
 React/Vue/  Python/Node/   SQLite/PG/    any         Ollama, LM Studio
 Svelte/HTML Java/C++/Go…   external…
```

- **The shell is not your app.** It is the runtime and management layer around it. Your frontend and backend stay
  normal, independent projects – change them (by hand or by an agent) and the running app picks it up. The shell is
  never rebuilt.
- **Free choice of building blocks.** Frontend, backend, database and functions for AI agents are independent:
  build a UI that stores data without a backend, an AI interface over a database without any UI, a pure background
  service – or everything together. See [building blocks](docs/building-blocks.md).
- **One config file** describes the app: which frontend to show, which services to run, how to check their health,
  what agents may do. See the [configuration reference](docs/configuration.md).
- **One runtime, three modes:** development (hot reload, broad agent access), production (stable, restricted agents)
  and headless (no window, background service).

## Using OpenShell

### Turn an existing web app into a desktop app

```bash
cd my-existing-project
openshell init        # detects Vite/Next/CRA/Angular/Vue frontends and Python/Node/Go/Rust/Java/C++ backends
openshell doctor      # checks commands, folders, ports, toolchain
openshell dev
```

A typical `openshell.json`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "app": { "name": "My App", "version": "1.0.0", "icon": "assets/icon.png" },
  "frontend": {
    "command": "npm run dev -- --port ${port} --strictPort",
    "cwd": "frontend",
    "port": "auto",
    "url": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}",
    "setup": { "command": "npm install", "creates": "frontend/node_modules" },
    "build": "npm run build",
    "dist": "frontend/dist",
    "proxy": { "/api": "${services.backend.url}" },
    "depends_on": ["backend"]
  },
  "services": [
    {
      "name": "backend",
      "command": ["python", "main.py"],
      "cwd": "backend",
      "port": "auto",
      "healthcheck": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/health",
      "openapi": "/openapi.json",
      "watch": ["backend"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Your backend reads its port from `PORT`, stores data in `OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR` and answers `/health`. That is the whole
contract – see the [app contract](docs/ai/app-development.md#the-app-contract).

### Develop

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Run with window / without window (browser) | `openshell dev` / `openshell dev --headless` |
| What is running? (state, pid, port, CPU, memory) | `openshell status` |
| Logs | `openshell logs backend -f --errors` |
| Restart / stop / start a service | `openshell restart backend` · `openshell stop worker` · `openshell run worker` |
| Production mode, in the background | `openshell start --detach` |
| Stop everything | `openshell stop` |

In the window, **right-click the title bar** (Windows) or use the **tray icon** to monitor every service – state, CPU,
memory, uptime – and to restart services, open logs or copy the MCP command for agents.

### Any language

| Backend | Example `command` | `build` |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `["python", "main.py"]` | – |
| Node.js | `["node", "server.js"]` | – |
| Java / Spring Boot | `["mvnw", "spring-boot:run"]` | – (or `mvnw package` + `java -jar`) |
| C++ (CMake) | `["build/bin/server"]` | `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build` |
| Go / Rust / .NET | `["bin/server"]` | `go build` / `cargo build` / `dotnet build` |

Compiled services rebuild and restart automatically on every change in development mode. Details:
[docs/languages.md](docs/languages.md).

### Ship

`openshell package` builds the app (`frontend.build`, `services[].build`) and creates a native installer with your
app's name and icon – NSIS/MSI on Windows, `.app`/`.dmg` on macOS, `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.AppImage` on Linux. Installed apps
keep their data per user and are MCP servers themselves. See [docs/installers.md](docs/installers.md).

## AI agents

OpenShell offers agents two profiles over [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (and plain HTTP/JSON):

| | **App profile** – *use* the app | **Full profile** – *develop* the app |
|---|---|---|
| For | assistants working with your application | coding agents building / fixing it |
| Tools | the app's own functions: declared capabilities, imported OpenAPI operations, frontend actions, `app_status` | 32 tools: status, logs, services, files, UI automation, tasks, capabilities |
| Connect | `openshell mcp --app --start` · installed app: `my-app.exe --mcp` | `openshell mcp` |

```bash
claude mcp add my-app     -- openshell mcp --app --start --project /path/to/my-app   # use
claude mcp add my-app-dev -- openshell mcp --project /path/to/my-app                 # develop
```

Every call is checked against permission scopes (`read`, `ui`, `actions`, `services`, `files`, `code`, `system`),
critical actions can require a human approval dialog, and everything is written to an audit log.
Read more in [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md).

### Build a new app with an AI coding agent

This repository is prepared for AI harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Aider, …):

- [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) / [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) – entry points for agents working in this repo,
- [`docs/ai/app-development.md`](docs/ai/app-development.md) – the complete guide for building apps on OpenShell
  (also printed by `openshell guide`),
- [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) / [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) – the documentation in LLM-friendly form,
- every project created with `openshell create` / `openshell init` gets its own `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.

So you can simply say to your coding agent:

> *Build me a desktop app with OpenShell: a recipe manager with a React frontend and a Python backend. Recipes should
> be searchable, and AI agents should be able to add and find recipes.*

The agent finds the contract, the templates, the verification commands (`openshell status`, `openshell call
ui_snapshot`, …) and the packaging steps on its own. See [docs/ai/README.md](docs/ai/README.md).

## Features

- **Building blocks** – frontend, backend, built-in SQLite database (migrations, SDK and agent access) and script
  functions for AI agents; combine freely with `openshell create --with …` / `openshell add …`. Apps without a
  frontend get a console window (services, data browser, functions) or run tray-only.
- **Runtime manager** – dependency-ordered start, one-time setup (`npm install`), build steps, HTTP/TCP health checks,
  restart policies with backoff and crash-loop protection, dynamic ports and `${services.x.url}` variables, logs,
  CPU/memory per process tree, process-tree cleanup (Windows job objects, Unix process groups), external services.
- **Frontend manager** – dev servers with HMR, production builds served by OpenShell with `/api` reverse proxy,
  external URLs; framework-agnostic.
- **Desktop integration** – window settings, loading screen, runtime panel, tray, notifications, close-to-tray /
  background mode, single instance, title-bar service menu, approval dialogs.
- **Agent Interaction Layer** – MCP (stdio + Streamable HTTP) and HTTP/JSON, semantic UI automation (accessibility-style
  snapshots with element refs, click/fill/press/navigate/wait), capabilities from config / OpenAPI / frontend SDK,
  AI provider discovery (Ollama, LM Studio, configured providers).
- **Security** – permission scopes per mode, human approvals, append-only audit log, project-scoped file access,
  loopback-only control API with tokens, Host and Origin checks.
- **Developer experience** – CLI (`init`, `create`, `dev`, `doctor`, `logs`, `package`, …), 8 templates, JSON Schema
  for editor completion, frontend SDK, `openshell doctor`.
- **Installers** – per-app branded installers without compiling desktop code.

## Project status

**Alpha (0.1).** Tested end to end on Windows 11: desktop shell, services in Python / Node / Java / C++, monitoring,
CLI, MCP in both profiles, OpenAPI import, UI automation, approvals, NSIS installers. macOS and Linux build in CI but
have seen little manual testing. APIs and the config format may still change before 1.0. Next: bundled runtimes,
auto-updates, code signing, screenshot fallback for UI automation – see the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md).

## Repository layout

```
apps/desktop/      openshell-desktop  Tauri 2 shell: window, WebView, tray, menus, dialogs, loading screen
crates/config      openshell-config   config schema, parsing, validation, variables
crates/runtime     openshell-runtime  services, health, builds, logs, metrics, static server, file watching
crates/agent       openshell-agent    permissions, approvals, audit, UI bridge, tool catalogue, MCP protocol
crates/core        openshell-core     runtime + agent layer, control API, tools, OpenAPI import, MCP stdio
crates/cli         openshell          command line interface
crates/package     openshell-package  native installers
packages/sdk       @openshell/sdk     optional frontend SDK
templates/         project templates (embedded into the CLI)
examples/          runnable examples
docs/              documentation (docs/ai: material for AI agents, docs/concept: original concept, German)
schema/            JSON Schema of openshell.json
```

# Building apps on OpenShell – guide for AI coding agents

This guide is written for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Aider, custom agents) that are asked
to **build a new desktop application with OpenShell** or to extend an existing OpenShell app. It is self-contained:
follow it top to bottom. The same text is printed by `openshell guide`.

## What OpenShell is (in one paragraph)

OpenShell is a desktop shell (Rust + Tauri 2) that runs a web frontend in a native window and supervises any number of
backend processes. An application is **not compiled into the shell**: it is a normal project folder with a web
frontend, one or more services (any language) and an `openshell.json` that describes them. You write the application;
OpenShell starts it, checks health, restarts on crashes, reloads on file changes, collects logs, packages installers
and exposes the app to AI agents over MCP.

## The app contract

Everything an app must do – nothing more:

| # | Rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every service that listens reads its port from the **`PORT`** environment variable and binds to **`127.0.0.1`**. Use `"port": "auto"` in the config. | Ports are assigned by OpenShell; no conflicts between apps. |
| 2 | HTTP services answer **`GET /health`** with `200` (configure `"healthcheck": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/health"`). | Readiness and dependency ordering. |
| 3 | Persistent data goes to **`OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR`** (fallback for running without OpenShell: a local `data/` folder). Never write into the project/install folder at runtime. | Installed apps live in read-only or replaced folders; the data dir is per user. |
| 4 | Log to **stdout/stderr**, one line per event, unbuffered (Python gets `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` automatically; flush in Java/C++). | Logs are shown in the terminal, the runtime panel and to agents. |
| 5 | The frontend calls the backend via **relative URLs** (`/api/...`). Static frontends: `"proxy": {"/api": "${services.backend.url}"}`; dev servers (Vite): proxy `/api` to `process.env.BACKEND_URL` and set `"env": {"BACKEND_URL": "${services.backend.url}"}`. | Same code works in dev, production and in a browser. |
| 6 | Expose the app's functions to agents as **capabilities** (config, OpenAPI or frontend actions) – see below. | Agents can *use* the app without UI automation. |
| 7 | The frontend works without OpenShell too: guard SDK usage with `if (window.__OPENSHELL__)`. | Browser mode, tests. |

## Workflow

### 1. Check the environment

```bash
openshell --version          # CLI available?
openshell doctor             # in a project: config, commands, ports, toolchain
openshell create --list      # available templates
```

If `openshell` is missing, tell the user to install it (see the OpenShell README) – do not try to re-implement it.

### 2. Choose the building blocks (new app), a template, or `init` (existing web app)

An app needs **only the blocks the task requires** – frontend, backend, database, functions for AI agents
(docs/building-blocks.md). Pick the smallest set:

| User wants | Blocks |
|---|---|
| A UI that stores data locally | `frontend,database` (the page uses `OpenShell.db`; no backend) |
| Tools/an AI interface for agents, no UI | `functions` (+ `database` if data must persist) |
| An API / background service | `backend` (+ `database`) |
| A full app | `frontend,backend,database` (+ `functions`) |

```bash
openshell create <name> --with frontend,database --lang python   # compose; files + openshell.json + AGENTS.md
openshell add function <name>                                    # add blocks later, in any order
openshell add database [name] | openshell add backend --lang node | openshell add frontend
```

Use a framework template when the user wants a specific stack:

| User wants | Template |
|---|---|
| Simple app, no build tools, fastest start | `vanilla-python` (HTML/JS + Python stdlib) |
| React UI | `react-python` or `react-node` |
| Vue / Svelte UI | `vue-python` / `svelte-go` |
| Java backend | `vanilla-java` (javac) – Spring Boot: start from `vanilla-java`, switch the service to `mvnw spring-boot:run` (see docs/languages.md) |
| C++ backend | `vanilla-cpp` (CMake) |
| Something else | `custom`, then fill in `openshell.json` |

```bash
openshell create <name> --template <template>     # creates <name>/ with AGENTS.md for you
# or, in an existing project:
openshell init                                    # writes openshell.json (+ AGENTS.md if missing)
```

Python backends in templates use only the standard library on purpose. If you need packages (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, …),
add a `requirements.txt` and a setup step: `"setup": { "command": "python -m pip install -r requirements.txt",
"creates": "<marker>" }`, or a venv (`python -m venv .venv` + `.venv/Scripts/python` / `.venv/bin/python` as command).

### 3. Run it and keep it running

```bash
openshell dev --headless     # no window; prints the URL. Use this when you (the agent) drive the app.
openshell dev                # with the native window (when the user is watching)
```

Run it **in the background** (it blocks). Then verify:

```bash
openshell status             # every service must be "running"
openshell logs --errors      # stderr + runtime messages
openshell logs backend -n 50
```

While it runs, OpenShell restarts services whose `watch` paths change and reloads static frontends – **do not restart
manually after every edit**; check `openshell status` / `openshell logs` instead. Compiled services (Java/C++) rebuild
automatically; a failing build shows the service as `failed` with compiler output in the logs and retries on the next
change.

### 4. Implement features

- Backend first (endpoint + `/health` stays green), then frontend, then capabilities.
- After each step: `openshell status`, `openshell logs --errors`, and exercise the endpoint:
  `curl` the service URL from `openshell status`, or call a capability: `openshell call cap_<name> '<json>'`.

### 5. Verify the UI like a user

With the app running (window or a browser tab on the printed URL for static frontends):

```bash
openshell call ui_snapshot                                   # page text + interactive elements with refs (e1, e2, …)
openshell call ui_fill '{"label": "Title", "value": "Test", "submit": true}'
openshell call ui_click '{"text": "Save"}'                   # or {"ref": "e7"}
openshell call ui_wait_for '{"text": "Saved"}'
openshell call ui_read_text '{"selector": "#list"}'
```

Notes: the UI bridge is injected into the desktop window and into pages served by OpenShell's static server. For dev
server frontends (Vite) in `--headless` mode it is not injected – verify through the API/capabilities instead, or run
`openshell dev` with the window.

If you are connected over MCP (full profile: `openshell mcp`), the same tools exist as MCP tools.

### 6. Make the app usable for agents (capabilities)

Design capabilities like a small, task-oriented API: verbs, clear descriptions, JSON Schema inputs, `read` for
queries and `actions` for changes. Four ways:

**0) Script functions** – no server needed (`openshell add function <name>` scaffolds one): a script reads a JSON
object from stdin and prints JSON to stdout; declare it with `"run": ["python", "tools/<name>.py"]`. Use the database
from scripts through `OPENSHELL_DB_<NAME>`. Errors: message on stderr + non-zero exit. Logs: `openshell logs fn:<name>`.


**a) Declared in `openshell.json`** (HTTP endpoint or task):

```json
"capabilities": [
  {
    "name": "add_item",
    "description": "Create an item. Returns the created item with its id.",
    "permission": "actions",
    "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "title": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["title"] },
    "http": { "service": "backend", "method": "POST", "path": "/api/items" }
  }
]
```

GET/DELETE send the input as query parameters, other methods as JSON body.

**b) OpenAPI import** – if the backend has an OpenAPI 3 JSON document (FastAPI `/openapi.json`, Spring springdoc
`/v3/api-docs`, ASP.NET `/swagger/v1/swagger.json`): `"openapi": "/openapi.json"` on the service. Give operations
meaningful `operationId`s and summaries – they become tool names and descriptions. Filter with
`{"location": "/openapi.json", "include": ["items"], "exclude": ["internal"]}`.

**c) Frontend actions** for UI-level functions:

```js
if (window.__OPENSHELL__) {
  const { OpenShell } = await import(`${window.__OPENSHELL__.api}/sdk.js`);
  OpenShell.agent.registerAction("open_item", {
    description: "Show an item in the editor",
    permission: "ui",
    input_schema: { type: "object", properties: { id: { type: "integer" } }, required: ["id"] },
  }, ({ id }) => openItem(id));
}
```

Check: `openshell call capabilities_list`, then test each with `openshell call cap_<name> '<json>'`. Agents that use
the app connect with `openshell mcp --app` and see exactly these functions.

### 7. Production check and packaging

```bash
openshell stop
openshell build              # frontend.build + services[].build
openshell start --headless   # production mode (static dist, no file watching, restricted agent permissions)
openshell status && openshell stop
openshell package            # native installer (needs app.version as semver, optional app.icon PNG)
```

## `openshell.json` cheat sheet

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "app": { "name": "Notes", "id": "com.example.notes", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "…", "icon": "icon.png" },
  "window": { "width": 1200, "height": 800, "min_width": 600, "min_height": 400 },

  // frontend: dev server (command+url), static files (dist) or external url
  "frontend": {
    "command": "npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${port} --strictPort",
    "cwd": "frontend", "port": "auto", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}",
    "env": { "BACKEND_URL": "${services.backend.url}" },
    "setup": { "command": "npm install", "creates": "frontend/node_modules" },
    "build": "npm run build", "dist": "frontend/dist",          // production: OpenShell serves dist
    "proxy": { "/api": "${services.backend.url}" },             // used by the static server
    "depends_on": ["backend"]
  },

  "services": [
    {
      "name": "backend",                                        // [a-z0-9_-], "frontend" is reserved
      "command": ["python", "main.py"],                         // argv, or a shell string "npm start"
      "cwd": "backend",
      "port": "auto",                                           // -> $PORT, ${port}, ${services.backend.url}
      "healthcheck": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/health",
      "build": ["javac", "-d", "build/classes", "src/Main.java"],  // compiled languages; dev: before every start
      "openapi": "/openapi.json",
      "env": { "LOG_LEVEL": "info" },
      "restart": true,                                          // on-failure (default) | "always" | false
      "watch": ["backend"],                                     // dev: restart on change
      "depends_on": ["db"]
    },
    { "name": "db", "external": true, "healthcheck": { "tcp": "127.0.0.1:5432" } }
  ],

  "capabilities": [ /* see above */ ],
  "tasks": { "test": "pytest", "migrate": "python manage.py migrate" },   // agents: task_run (scope "system")
  "agents": {
    "permissions": { "development": ["read","ui","actions","services","files","code"], "production": ["read","ui","actions"] },
    "approval_required": ["system"]
  },
  "package": { "exclude": ["docs"], "targets": ["nsis"] }
}
```

Variables: `${port}`, `${services.<name>.port|url}`, `${frontend.url}`, `${project.root}`, `${mode}`, `${env.NAME}`.
Env vars every service gets: `PORT`, `OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR`, `OPENSHELL_MODE`, `OPENSHELL_SERVICE`,
`OPENSHELL_PROJECT_ROOT`, `OPENSHELL_CONTROL_URL`. Full reference: `openshell schema` or docs/configuration.md.

## Databases

`databases: [{ "name": "main", "migrations": "db/migrations", "agent_access": "write" }]` gives the app a SQLite file
in `OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR`. Schema changes: add `db/migrations/002_….sql` (never edit applied migrations; they run once,
in order, at startup). Access: services/functions `OPENSHELL_DB_MAIN` (+ `DATABASE_URL`), frontend `OpenShell.db.query
/ execute` (needs `actions` in `agents.sdk_permissions` to write), agents `db_query` / `db_execute`. Inspect with
`openshell call db_list`, `openshell call db_query '{"sql": "SELECT …"}'` or the console's data browser.

## Pitfalls

- **Hard-coded ports** (`8000`, `5173`) → conflicts. Use `"port": "auto"` and `$PORT`.
- **Binding to `0.0.0.0` or `localhost`** → use `127.0.0.1` (the health check and proxy use it; `localhost` may resolve to `::1`).
- **Writing data next to the code** in a watched folder → endless restarts in dev mode and lost data in installed apps. Use `OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR`.
- **Buffered output** in Java/C++/Python without OpenShell → empty logs. Flush.
- **Vite without `--strictPort`** silently picks another port → the window loads the wrong URL.
- **Absolute URLs to the backend in the frontend** → break in production. Use `/api` + proxy.
- **`frontend.dist` must exist for production** → run `openshell build`.
- **Installing global tools** or changing the user's system is not needed; templates have no dependencies except the language runtime and (for Vite templates) `npm install`, which OpenShell runs itself via `setup`.
- **Do not edit `.openshell/`** – it is runtime state (logs, audit log, `runtime.json` with the control token).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Only the building blocks the task needs (no backend just to store data, no UI for a pure agent tool)
- [ ] `openshell doctor` shows no errors
- [ ] `openshell dev --headless` → `openshell status`: all services `running`; `openshell logs --errors` clean
- [ ] Main user flows verified through the API and, where possible, `ui_snapshot` / `ui_click` / `ui_fill`
- [ ] Capabilities for the app's main functions; each tested with `openshell call cap_<name>`
- [ ] Data stored in `OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR`
- [ ] Production check: `openshell build` + `openshell start --headless` works
- [ ] `README.md` of the app explains how to run it (`openshell dev`) and what agents can do
- [ ] Optional: `openshell package` produces an installer

## Reference

| Need | Where |
|---|---|
| All config fields | `openshell schema`, docs/configuration.md |
| Agent tools, permissions, MCP | docs/agents.md, `openshell tools` |
| Languages (Java, C++, Go, Rust, .NET) | docs/languages.md |
| Installers | docs/installers.md |
| Frontend SDK | docs/sdk.md, `<control_url>/sdk.js` |
| HTTP control API | docs/control-api.md |

# Getting started

## 1. Install

OpenShell consists of two binaries:

- `openshell` – the CLI (also runs the headless runtime and the MCP server)
- `openshell-desktop` – the desktop shell (Tauri 2)

**Prebuilt binaries** (from the [releases page](https://github.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA/releases)):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA/main/scripts/install.sh | sh     # macOS / Linux
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex         # Windows (PowerShell)
```

**From source** (needed until the first release is published, and for development):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RobinsSuperSchmiede/EDA.git
cd EDA
cargo build --release
```

Put `target/release` on your `PATH` (both binaries must be in the same directory, or set `OPENSHELL_DESKTOP` to the
desktop binary). Check your environment:

```bash
openshell doctor
```

## 2a. New project

```bash
openshell create my-app                         # HTML/JS + Python stdlib, no installs
openshell create my-app --template react-python # React (Vite) + Python
openshell create --list                         # show all templates
cd my-app
openshell dev
```

## 2b. Existing project

```bash
cd my-existing-project
openshell init        # detects frontend (Vite, Next, CRA, Angular, Vue CLI, static) and backend (Python, Node, Go, Rust)
openshell doctor      # verifies commands, directories, ports
openshell dev
```

`init` writes a starting point – review the generated `openshell.json`, especially ports and health checks.
A typical configuration:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "app": { "name": "My App" },
  "frontend": {
    "command": "npm run dev -- --port ${port} --strictPort",
    "cwd": "frontend",
    "port": "auto",
    "url": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}",
    "setup": { "command": "npm install", "creates": "frontend/node_modules" },
    "build": "npm run build",
    "dist": "frontend/dist",
    "proxy": { "/api": "${services.backend.url}" },
    "env": { "BACKEND_URL": "${services.backend.url}" },
    "depends_on": ["backend"]
  },
  "services": [
    {
      "name": "backend",
      "command": ["python", "main.py"],
      "cwd": "backend",
      "port": "auto",
      "healthcheck": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/health",
      "restart": true,
      "watch": ["backend"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Your backend reads its port from the `PORT` environment variable. The frontend dev server proxies `/api` to
`BACKEND_URL`; in production OpenShell serves `frontend/dist` itself and proxies `/api`.

## 3. Run

| Command | What happens |
|---|---|
| `openshell dev` | Development mode: window, file watching, broad agent permissions, logs in the terminal. |
| `openshell dev --headless` | Same without a window – open the printed URL in your browser (browser mode). |
| `openshell start` | Production mode (uses `frontend.dist` when configured). |
| `openshell start --headless --detach` | Background runtime without window. |
| `openshell status` / `logs -f` / `restart backend` / `stop` | Manage the running app from another terminal. |

While `openshell dev` runs:

- edit backend files → the backend restarts (`watch`),
- edit frontend files → the dev server hot-reloads, or OpenShell reloads the window for static frontends,
- a crashing service is restarted with backoff; after 5 crashes per minute it is marked `failed`,
- `openshell build` + `openshell start` runs the production build.

## 4. Connect an AI agent

Coding agents: every project created with `openshell create` / `openshell init` contains an `AGENTS.md`, and
`openshell guide` prints the complete guide for building OpenShell apps. To connect an agent to the running app:

```bash
claude mcp add my-app-dev -- openshell mcp --project /path/to/my-app              # develop the app
claude mcp add my-app     -- openshell mcp --app --start --project /path/to/my-app  # use the app
```

See [agents.md](agents.md) for other agents, the tool list and permissions.


================================================================================
FILE: docs/building-blocks.md
================================================================================

# Building blocks: build only what you need

An OpenShell app is assembled from four independent building blocks. Every block is optional – use one, several or
all of them:

| Block | What it is | Add it |
|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | A web UI in the native window (static files, a dev server or a URL) | `openshell add frontend` |
| **Backend** | An HTTP service in any language, supervised by OpenShell | `openshell add backend [--lang python\|node]` |
| **Database** | A built-in SQLite database with migrations, managed by OpenShell | `openshell add database [name]` |
| **Functions** | Functions for AI agents (MCP tools) implemented as scripts – no server | `openshell add function <name> [--lang python\|node]` |

Start a new app with any combination:

```bash
openshell create my-app --with frontend,database          # UI that stores data – no backend
openshell create my-app --with database,functions         # an AI interface over a database – no UI, no server
openshell create my-app --with backend                    # a supervised API service
openshell create my-app --with frontend,backend,database,functions
openshell create my-app                                   # in a terminal: asks which blocks you want
```

Blocks can be added later in any order; they connect themselves (a frontend added to an app with a backend proxies
`/api` to it, the backend receives the database path, the frontend gets write access to the database, …).

## Typical combinations

| You want | Blocks | How it works |
|---|---|---|
| A desktop UI with local storage | frontend + database | The page uses `OpenShell.db.query/execute` from the [SDK](sdk.md). |
| An AI interface to your data | database + functions | Agents get your functions plus `db_query` / `db_execute` (as allowed by `agent_access`). |
| Tools for AI agents only | functions | Each function is a script: JSON in, JSON out. The app has no UI and no server. |
| A background service | backend | Runs headless or in the tray (`"window": {"enabled": false}`). |
| A classic web app as desktop app | frontend + backend (+ database) | As before; the backend can use `OPENSHELL_DB_MAIN`. |

Apps **without a frontend** show OpenShell's console in the window: services, databases (with a data browser),
functions (with a "Run" button), logs and the commands to connect AI agents. Set `"window": {"enabled": false}` to
run only in the tray instead.

## Frontend

```json
"frontend": { "dist": "web", "watch": ["web"] }
```

Any frontend works – static files, a Vite/Next dev server (`command` + `url`) or an external URL; see
[configuration.md](configuration.md#frontend). The starter page from `openshell add frontend` adapts to the other
blocks: it shows a backend call, a notes list from the database and the app's functions.

## Backend

```json
{
  "name": "backend",
  "command": ["python", "main.py"],
  "cwd": "backend",
  "port": "auto",
  "healthcheck": "http://127.0.0.1:${port}/health",
  "watch": ["backend"]
}
```

Any language ([languages.md](languages.md)). Read `PORT`, bind `127.0.0.1`, answer `/health`.

## Database

```json
"databases": [
  { "name": "main", "migrations": "db/migrations", "agent_access": "write" }
]
```

- **File**: `<name>.db` in the app's data directory (`OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR`, per user for installed apps). Override
  with `"path"` (relative to the data directory, or absolute).
- **Migrations**: every `*.sql` file in `migrations` is applied once, in file-name order, inside a transaction.
  Add new files (`002_add_tags.sql`) – never edit applied ones.
- **Services and functions** get the path as `OPENSHELL_DB_<NAME>` (e.g. `OPENSHELL_DB_MAIN`) and the main database
  as `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///…`. Any SQLite library works (Python `sqlite3`, `better-sqlite3`, JDBC, …).
- **Frontend**: `OpenShell.db.query(sql, params)` / `OpenShell.db.execute(sql, params)`. Writing needs `actions` in
  `agents.sdk_permissions` (`openshell add` sets it).
- **Agents**: `db_list`, `db_schema`, `db_query` (read-only, enforced by SQLite) and `db_execute`, controlled per
  database by `agent_access`: `none`, `read` (default) or `write`. The schema is also an MCP resource
  (`openshell://db/<name>/schema`).
- WAL mode and a busy timeout are set, so the shell, services and functions can use the file at the same time.
- The console's data browser shows every table.

PostgreSQL, MySQL & co. run as services (`"external": true` with a TCP health check, or a container command) and are
used from your backend.

## Functions

```json
"capabilities": [
  {
    "name": "summarize_notes",
    "description": "Summarize all open notes",
    "permission": "read",
    "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "limit": { "type": "integer" } } },
    "run": ["python", "tools/summarize_notes.py"]
  }
]
```

```python
import json, os, sqlite3, sys

args = json.load(sys.stdin)                       # input object
con = sqlite3.connect(os.environ["OPENSHELL_DB_MAIN"])
rows = con.execute("SELECT title FROM notes WHERE done = 0 LIMIT ?", (args.get("limit", 20),)).fetchall()
print(json.dumps({"open": [r[0] for r in rows]})) # result
```

- Input: JSON object on stdin (also in `OPENSHELL_INPUT`). Output: JSON or text on stdout. Errors: message on stderr
  and a non-zero exit code. `"run": {"command": …, "cwd": …, "env": {…}, "timeout_ms": 60000}` for more control.
- Any language: `["node", "tools/x.mjs"]`, `["java", "-cp", "build", "Tool"]`, a compiled binary, …
- Agents see functions as MCP tools in the app profile (`openshell mcp --app`) under their own names, and as
  `cap_<name>` in the developer profile. The frontend calls them with `OpenShell.invoke(name, input)`, the console
  has a "Run" button, the CLI `openshell call cap_<name> '<json>'`.
- `stderr` output is in the logs (`openshell logs fn:<name>`).

Other function sources, also listed as capabilities: HTTP endpoints of a backend (`"http"`), declared tasks
(`"task"`), operations imported from an OpenAPI document (`"openapi"` on a service) and actions registered by the
frontend (`OpenShell.agent.registerAction`). See [agents.md](agents.md#capabilities-the-applications-own-functions).


================================================================================
FILE: docs/tutorial.md
================================================================================

# Tutorial: build a complete OpenShell app

In about 20 minutes you build **Bookmarks**, a small desktop app with a Python backend and a plain HTML frontend,
make it usable for AI agents and package it as an installer. Everything here works the same with the React, Vue,
Svelte, Java or C++ templates.

Prerequisites: `openshell` and `openshell-desktop` on your `PATH` ([getting started](getting-started.md)), Python 3.

## 1. Create the project

```bash
openshell create bookmarks
cd bookmarks
openshell dev
```

A window opens with the template's todo list. The terminal shows the logs of both services:

```
 backend │ starting: python main.py
 backend │ ready after 0.4s
frontend │ serving …/web at http://127.0.0.1:53121/
```

Leave it running. The project looks like this:

```
openshell.json      what OpenShell runs (open it – it is short)
backend/main.py     JSON API, Python standard library
web/                index.html, app.js, style.css – served by OpenShell, /api is proxied to the backend
AGENTS.md           instructions for AI coding agents (see step 6)
```

## 2. Add a backend endpoint

Replace the todo logic in `backend/main.py` with bookmarks. The essentials of the OpenShell contract are already in
the template:

```python
PORT = int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8000"))                       # OpenShell assigns the port
DATA_DIR = os.environ.get("OPENSHELL_DATA_DIR") or "../data"     # per-app data directory
# ...
if path == "/health":                                            # health check used by OpenShell
    return self.send_json(200, {"status": "ok"})
```

Add two routes (sketch):

```python
if path == "/api/bookmarks" and self.command == "GET":
    q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query).get("q", [""])[0].lower()
    items = [b for b in load() if q in b["title"].lower() or q in b["url"].lower()]
    return self.send_json(200, items)

if path == "/api/bookmarks" and self.command == "POST":
    body = self.read_json()
    item = {"id": next_id(), "title": body["title"], "url": body["url"]}
    save(load() + [item])
    return self.send_json(201, item)
```

Save the file: the log shows `files changed: backend\main.py` → `restarting` → `ready`. If you made a mistake, the
error is in `openshell logs backend --errors` and the service restarts again on the next save.

## 3. Update the frontend

Edit `web/index.html` and `web/app.js` to list `GET /api/bookmarks` and post new ones. On save, OpenShell reloads the
window (`"watch": ["web"]` in the config). With a dev server template (React/Vue/Svelte) the dev server hot-reloads
instead.

Useful while developing:

```bash
openshell status                 # state, pid, port, CPU, memory of each service
openshell logs -f                # follow all logs
openshell restart backend
```

Right-click the window's title bar (Windows) or use the tray icon for the same overview.

## 4. Make the app usable for AI agents

Agents should be able to *use* Bookmarks without clicking through the UI. Declare its functions as **capabilities**
in `openshell.json`:

```json
"capabilities": [
  {
    "name": "search_bookmarks",
    "description": "Search bookmarks by text in title or URL",
    "permission": "read",
    "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "q": { "type": "string" } } },
    "http": { "service": "backend", "method": "GET", "path": "/api/bookmarks" }
  },
  {
    "name": "add_bookmark",
    "description": "Save a bookmark",
    "permission": "actions",
    "input_schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": { "title": { "type": "string" }, "url": { "type": "string" } },
      "required": ["title", "url"]
    },
    "http": { "service": "backend", "method": "POST", "path": "/api/bookmarks" }
  }
]
```

Try them right away:

```bash
openshell call cap_add_bookmark '{"title": "Tauri", "url": "https://tauri.app"}'
openshell call cap_search_bookmarks '{"q": "tauri"}'
```

Alternatives:

- **OpenAPI:** if your backend publishes an OpenAPI document (FastAPI does at `/openapi.json`), set
  `"openapi": "/openapi.json"` on the service instead – every endpoint becomes a capability automatically.
- **Frontend actions:** UI-only functions (e.g. "show the bookmarks of folder X") can be registered from the page with
  `OpenShell.agent.registerAction(...)` – see the template's `web/app.js` and the [SDK](sdk.md).

## 5. Connect an assistant

```bash
claude mcp add bookmarks -- openshell mcp --app --start --project /path/to/bookmarks
```

Ask: *"Save https://modelcontextprotocol.io as 'MCP spec' in my bookmarks."* The assistant sees exactly
`app_status`, `search_bookmarks` and `add_bookmark` – nothing else. With `--start`, the app is started in the
background if it is not running.

To let a coding agent work *on* the app, connect the full profile instead: `openshell mcp --project …`
([agents.md](agents.md)).

## 6. Let an AI coding agent extend the app

The project contains an `AGENTS.md` (and `CLAUDE.md`) that tells coding agents how OpenShell apps work, how to verify
changes (`openshell status`, `openshell call ui_snapshot`, `openshell logs --errors`) and how to expose new functions.
Open the folder in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, … and ask:

> *Add folders to the bookmarks app: each bookmark can be in a folder, the UI shows a folder list, and agents can
> list folders and move bookmarks.*

## 7. Ship it

Give the app a version and an icon in `openshell.json`:

```json
"app": { "name": "Bookmarks", "id": "com.example.bookmarks", "version": "1.0.0", "icon": "icon.png" }
```

```bash
openshell start            # try production mode first
openshell package          # → .openshell/package/bin/bundle/nsis/Bookmarks_1.0.0_x64-setup.exe (Windows)
```

The installed app stores its data in the user's data directory, runs in production mode (agents get only
`read`, `ui` and `actions` by default) and can be used by agents with `bookmarks.exe --mcp`.
More in [installers.md](installers.md).

## Where to go next

- [Configuration reference](configuration.md) – databases as external services, workers, tasks, proxies, modes
- [Languages](languages.md) – Java/Spring Boot, C++/CMake, Go, Rust, .NET backends
- [Agents](agents.md) – permissions, approvals, UI automation, audit log
